task: Should the box fall, make your very next move the one that picks it back up. If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands.

calls.candidate: hard Existence(at_exit), hard Precedence(holding_box, at_exit), hard Response(box_fell, holding_box)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: two mismatches. (1) 'Should the box fall, make your very next move the one that picks it back up' requires ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box), not Response(box_fell, holding_box): the task demands the pickup on the very next step, which the Response drops. (2) 'If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands' is an if-sentence: at_exit is a condition, not a commanded goal, and the requirement is Response(at_exit, holding_box) hard. The clauses Existence(at_exit) hard and Precedence(holding_box, at_exit) hard are wrong: Precedence(holding_box, at_exit) says only that at_exit may not happen before the first holding_box, which is trivially true from step 1 and does not require the box at the exit, while Existence(at_exit) turns a conditional into an unconditional goal. Remove both and add Response(at_exit, holding_box) hard.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box), hard Existence(at_exit), hard Response(at_exit, holding_box)
calls.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(at_exit) hard captures the unconditional command to reach the exit; Response(at_exit, holding_box) hard matches 'if you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands' (an if-condition with a required consequent, correctly not an Existence on holding_box); ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) hard matches 'should the box fall, make your very next move the one that picks it back up', and since holding_box is true on the pickup step it closes as the task intends.
